mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4.5% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financing conditions affecting corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar rate hikes, or the 5-day moving average of SPX returns is non-negative during the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE exceeding 0.2 percentage points coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower expected wage growth reduces labor cost pressures and boosts equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 5-year window, the 60-day forward return is not statistically different from zero when UNRATE rises >0.2pp, or the correlation with SPX 60d returns is below -0.2.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) of at least 2% followed by a rebound in the next month predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates a resumption of growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls ≥2% in month t, then rises in month t+1
failure_condition: No significant positive 20d return occurs after such bounces in 80% of cases, or the 5-day SPX return is negative during the rebound window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% over three consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals robust supply-side expansion.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative in 60% of such supply expansions, or the 5-day average SPX return is negative during the expansion period.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 5-day forward return as low rates encourage risk-on positioning.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-positive in 80% of such periods, or the 10-day SPX return is not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (employment) of over 10,000 in a month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to increased unemployment risk and reduced consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by >10,000 in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in 70% of such events, or the 5-day SPX return is positive during the event window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% each month for two months triggers a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as dual demand weakness depresses equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 ↓2% and RSAFS ↓2% in the same month, for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are non-negative in 50% of such events, or the 20-day moving average SPX return is positive during the shock period.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-side expansion when INDPRO growth exceeds 5% for four consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates higher future profits.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO grows >5% monthly for 4 consecutive months (regime condition: post-inflationary supply shock)
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in 75% of such regimes, or the 5-day SPX return is negative during the expansion.
